set.approach: Park at the Worthington Glacier trailhead on the Thompson Pass side of the road and take the beaten path to the toe of the glacier. The climb starts right there and works up the glacier, with the slope steepening from moderate ice on the left to steeper ice farther right. Crevasses open up higher on the glacier.
set.descent_text: Parties descend by the moraine trail, which leads easily back down to the trailhead. A crevasse field higher up can be avoided by leaving the glacier onto the moraine, which gives an early way off.

review.notes: Single route page for approach and descent; no counts used.

set.approach: The route climbs a couloir on the east face of the unnamed peak that stands between Mt. Dickey and Mt. Bradley in the Ruth Gorge. Camps on the glacier floor put the base within a short approach.
set.descent_text: Parties who topped out chose not to reverse the couloir, because the snow flank at its top faces southeast and softens as the day warms. They went down the west face of the peak and crossed the pass beside it, then returned to the gorge floor on that side.

review.notes: One report supports the east-face couloir start and the west-face descent; stated grade there is AI5 and about 800 m, row says WI5 4 pitches.

set.approach: Leave a vehicle at the plowed pullout beside the Parks Highway, on its west side, and head west by ski or snowmachine to Cantwell Creek, then go up the drainage to the boundary of the Denali wilderness; snowmachines are left there and the rest of the way to the glacial moraine at the creek headwaters is on skis. The climb is on an east-northeast-facing wall, reached by a snow slope that ends at a flat spot above a house-sized boulder, then crossing a snow-filled chute to the rock where the first pitch starts. Rockfall potential is above average.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The last belay is at a small ice blob in a tight canyon where a thread can be built, with pitons in a crack on the left; a short rope may not reach that blob from the anchors below, so carry a long rope or climb up to it first.

review.notes: Single route page; no counts.

set.approach: Leave a vehicle at the plowed pullout beside the Parks Highway, on its west side, and ski or snowmachine up Cantwell Creek to the boundary of the Denali wilderness. Snowmachines are left at the boundary; skis cover the rest of the way to the glacial moraine at the headwaters. The climb is on an east-northeast-facing wall, partly hidden by a spine coming off the rocky face south of the glacier. Skirt the big snow bowl to reach the foot of the ice. The Cantwell Glacier above can shed seracs onto the route, and rockfall potential is above average.

review.notes: Single route page; no counts.

set.descent_text: Alder bushes beside the top of the climb can be used as a rappel anchor.

review.notes: Descent only; the page gives no approach.

set.descent_text: The steep ice steps are separated by flat walking, and the finish allows a walk-off.

review.notes: Descent only; page gives no approach.

set.approach: Parties start from the Kahiltna base camp airstrip and follow the West Buttress track to the lower camp, then leave it to ascend the Northeast Fork of that glacier. The start is a conspicuous couloir cutting the eastern flank of the rib. The Northeast Fork is exposed to hanging glaciers and avalanche terrain, so a common alternative is to climb the West Buttress to its higher camp and traverse across to the upper part of the rib, skipping the lower mountain.
set.descent_text: Parties usually descend the West Buttress after the summit. Food and fuel are often cached at the West Buttress camp for use on the way down. A shorter variant instead returns to the high camp on the rib and descends from there.

review.notes: Both pages agree on the Northeast Fork approach and West Buttress descent.

set.approach: The route is on the south face of Tiehacker Mountain, up Glacier Creek above Seward. Access is from the Bear Lake neighborhood by truck, sled, skis or on foot. The flow sits below a large Y-shaped funnel, so check the avalanche forecast and avoid it except at low hazard.
set.descent_text: Descend by V-thread rappels, or climb snow up to the ridge on Tiehacker and follow the summer trail down to the Bear Lake neighborhood.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek and follow it to where Godwin Creek joins. Continue up Godwin Creek past the forested rock buttress where Jailbreak is, and on for a few hundred yards more. The whole route cannot be seen from one place; look for a narrow, left-trending apron of ice falling out of the forested cliff beneath a large chimney system, and head uphill to the foot of that apron.
set.descent_text: The top of the route is the forested cliff rim. Descend using bolted anchors, trees and V-threads.

review.notes: Single route page. Loose rock noted there.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek and follow it to where Godwin Creek joins. Continue up Godwin Creek past the forested rock buttress holding Jailbreak, then a little farther to the apron of ice below a large chimney system, reached by heading uphill. The ice is mostly hidden from the creek. It lies on the north side of the drainage in the second big south-facing alcove.

review.notes: Approach from Blood Moon page, whose lower apron is this route; Mountain Project places it in the second south-facing alcove. No descent source.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek, follow it to the Godwin Creek confluence, and continue up Godwin Creek beyond Jailbreak and Blood Moon. The route begins by climbing the lower easy ice of Lunar Orbit, reached by bushwhacking uphill from the creek to the base of that low-angle ice.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the tree belay, or walk left through the trees to the short last pitch of Lunar Orbit.

review.notes: Descent from route page; approach combines its start on Lunar Orbit with that route page.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek and follow it up to where Godwin Creek comes in. Head up Godwin Creek to Jailbreak, the first big flow on the left in a large rock corner, reached by a steep scree and devil's club slope from the creek. Jailbait climbs Jailbreak's first pitches and then veers up and left. The route faces southwest and is near the ocean.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek and walk up it until Godwin Creek joins from the side. Head up Godwin Creek to the first major flow on the left, in a large rock corner. Reaching the base means climbing a steep slope of scree and devil's club from the creek.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Hike up the Godwin Creek drainage. Where it begins to narrow, before the canyon proper, look high and to the left for the upper part of the climb. Contour onto a hanging bench, where an old hunting trail may be found, and follow the forest uphill to a hanging drainage that leads to the base. The route is mostly hidden in old-growth forest above the lower canyon.

review.notes: No descent source.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek and follow it to the Godwin Creek confluence. Go up Godwin Creek past Jailbreak, on the west end of a forested rock buttress, and continue beyond Blood Moon. Judge your position from the creek bed, then bushwhack uphill to the gentler ice that runs down below the crux; the route is longer or shorter depending on snow depth.
set.descent_text: Descend from the trees using V-threads or a tree anchor.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Park at 4th of July Creek and follow it to the confluence with Godwin Creek. Go past Jailbreak and continue up Godwin Creek another quarter mile or so. The route is not visible as a whole from any one spot; look for a left-trending narrow ice apron coming out of the forested cliff below a big chimney system and walk uphill to its base. It shares this lower ice with Blood Moon.

review.notes: No descent stated. Occasional loose rock noted.

set.approach: Walk up Gunnysack Creek; it is a long slog, especially early in the season. Gunnysack 1 is passed first, a few thousand feet before this route. The one obstacle is a narrow part of the creek squeezed between boulders, where you scramble around either side because the ice there is rarely stable.
set.descent_text: At the top of the climb, either walk off to the left (the ground can be steep and icy) or rappel from a V-thread, which is probably the better choice.

review.notes: Page lists WI4, row WI3-4; same creek and coordinates.

set.approach: Park near the bridge over Gunnysack Creek and make the long walk up the creek. The first pitch is reached by a chossy corner to a cave, where you belay.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the top of the pillar, or finish the climb and walk off to climber's right down a big gully above Gunnysack 2, cutting right before the top of that route to return to the base of the ice.

review.notes: Single route page for descent.

set.approach: From the International Falls parking area, drop down and cross the river to the plateau under Feather. Follow the first fault line up to the basin of the Cleveland Glacier, then continue up the basin to the obvious cliff band.

review.notes: No descent stated; no times used.

set.approach: Parties reach the Mendenhall Towers by a short helicopter flight from Juneau, or on skis from the ridge north of the Mendenhall Glacier to its north branch, or directly up the glacier. For this line on the north face of the West Tower, follow the snow as high as possible and then trend left onto the face.

review.notes: Single page states the descent; area page for access.

set.approach: Cross the glacier along the west side of the towers, toward the rabbit ear and around big crevasses, to a small notch or gully just above the toe of the ridge. From that notch the route reaches the crest by way of the southern flank, above a gendarme.

review.notes: No descent stated on its own page.

set.approach: Parties fly from Talkeetna onto the glacier below the south face, and base camp is a short walk from the landing. From there it is a brief walk across the glacier to the base of the route, then across the bergschrund to start.
set.descent_text: Descend by reversing the route with rappels. Getting back to the glacier takes well over a dozen rappels.

review.notes: Skyward says 16-18 rappels, other says 18; stated as well over a dozen.

set.approach: Drive to the Eagle River Nature Center and hike the climber's trail to Icicle Creek; the trail is only sporadically marked and the bushwhack through alders is long. Avoid the cliffy lower creek by heading for the prominent buttress on the left, passing through a cottonwood grove, and using the gully at the base of the buttress. A large boulder at the mouth of the valley makes a common bivy. The route is on the northwest face, started by scrambling up lower-angle ground.
set.descent_text: After topping out on the 6,000-foot subpeak northeast of the true summit, parties hiked over it and descended the Icicle Glacier by the standard northeast ridge route.

review.notes: Approach: area page and AAJ report; descent from AAJ only.

set.approach: At Kahiltna Base Camp, drop down Heartbreak Hill and ski around the west side of Mt. Francis to enter the glacier's East Fork. The first feature on the right is Stubbs' Buttress, a small satellite off the northwest ridge, and the route climbs its north buttress.
set.descent_text: Downclimb from the summit toward the prominent ice gully, where a nut-and-pin anchor sits in a large rock. Rappel on rock gear to the ice gully, then make V-thread rappels to the base.

review.notes: Single route page; counts omitted.

set.approach: From the base camp airstrip, head northeast across crevassed glacier and follow the base of Mt. Francis to the foot of the Francis Saddle, from where the ridge is gained.
set.descent_text: Descend by reversing the route. Start early so you are not coming down the south-facing snow when it softens.

review.notes: Single page.
